stage_title: What production cars that wire this way do better — the agent's improvement list
item: A shorted MOSFET is an output stuck ON — decide what that means for each safety load (motorsport PDM practice)
note: Read 2026-09-12. The manual is silent, and definitively so: the PMU's entire output-status vocabulary is 0 OFF, 1 ACTIVE, 2 UNDERCURRENT, 3 OVERCURRENT, 7 THERMAL SHUTDOWN - every one a story about current through an output the module believes it is driving, and none of them 'commanded off and still live'. It IS inferable: each output's voltage is measured (0-16 V on the 25 A and 15 A pins, 0-20 V on the 7 A pins), so a function comparing oN.voltage against oN.active catches a shorted high-side switch - that is CK07, and it annunciates only, because the annunciator is the module that just failed. The hard kill is the master disconnect and recovery RC01 is that sentence, first, before any other step. Worth knowing and not in the row: the PMU has a built-in inertia switch that drops every output above a configurable acceleration threshold (6 G default) - which covers the crash case exactly as long as the module is alive, and a shorted FET is the case where it is not. The O5 series relay is Camden's, as the row said: block 00.15.

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Read the safety rules once, properly, before the first tool touches the car
note: The battery is lithium: boot or tape both terminals whenever you work, rings and watches off - a dropped tool welds. Open the master disconnect before touching the 2 AWG feed, the starter cable, the tank sender or the pop-up buckets. It is on the POSITIVE side (D-319), so opening it removes supply from everything, the starter cable included; before it is fitted, pull the negative lug. Jack stands always, wheels chocked (P is not a parking brake). No sparks near the tank; extinguisher within reach. Engine running: belt/fan clear, garage door open (CO). Pop-ups move fast and a stalled motor pulls 15-25 A. Label the factory end of every migrated circuit MIGRATED + date.

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Deutsch and heat-shrink practice on scrap
note: Insert and remove a contact from a spare housing ten times with the removal tool (P031/P032); fit and pull the wedgelock - a contact must click and not back out under a firm tug. Adhesive heat-shrink until the glue weeps evenly at both ends; one lug with heavy-wall shrink and a boot.

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Set up the label printer and print the node labels
note: Format: rules label-format. Print TEST / L0-X0, wrap it on a 16 AWG offcut, clear heat-shrink over it, tug it. Then print the node labels from the label columns: rx7.py sql 02-PROJECTS/01-electrical "select id,label from relays" and "select id,label from fuses".

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Build the ladder resistor sub-assemblies
note: Every resistor (and the one 1N5819) the ladders use, soldered to 4 in leads, each heat-shrunk and the lead labelled with switch and position; measure each and write the value on its bag. The list is the design, not this note: rx7.py sql 02-PROJECTS/01-electrical "select * from ladders" plus the cavity rows naming a kΩ value. Includes the 47 kOhm baselines: L2-S 1 and 2 (A4/A5), and new with D-368 L2-S 3 (A3), the sill splice (A6) and the hazard switch (A8). Do not fit the D-368 baselines in the car until CK12 has passed on the bench (A10 sizes the wake stages first).

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Backbone weekend, 1 of 5: the battery in the cargo bin
note: Disconnect the factory battery, negative first; boot the Ionic's terminals. Backing plate from the C1 (M-4) mock-up; hold-down through the floor with M8 grade-8, nyloc nuts, fender washers - never sheet metal alone. Fit battery and hold-down; push hard every way, it must not move (D2 fit-checked the parts).

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Backbone weekend, 2 of 5: disconnect, Class-T and the rear ground stud
note: Master disconnect within reach from the hatch, on the POSITIVE side (D-319). Class-T block as close to the positive post as physically possible - inches. Rear ground stud: bare metal, 3/8 stainless stud, star washer, torque, cavity wax over the joint. Cut and hydraulically crimp the battery cables exactly as rx7.py sql 02-PROJECTS/01-electrical "select * from backbone" and "select * from cables" route them (battery negative straight to the stud, B5); heavy-wall adhesive shrink and a boot on every lug.

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Backbone weekend, 3 of 5: starter run, PMU feed and grounds
note: MRBF holder on the positive post with the 250 A fuse (D-321), NOT fitted yet; 1/0 starter run to the starter B+ stud (D-246), loomed, P-clipped every 12 in, grommeted at every pass-through. 2 AWG PMU feed from the Class-T through the tunnel to a temporary insulated distribution post where the dash node will go - pull string in beside it before the console goes back. Front star stud on the radiator support (bare metal, stud, star washer, torque, wax) + 10 AWG BLK to a second body bolt. Engine block to chassis strap, 2 AWG, 24 in or less (the bond). 1/0 BLK cranking return from the rear stud to the block with the starter feed (D-246). MIDI holders F17/F18 beside the starter stud; alternator B+ through F18; F17 unwired until E38.

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Backbone weekend, 4 of 5: the factory harness onto the new backbone, then power
note: Move the factory harness's main feed (fusible-link side) onto the distribution post and its main ground onto the front star. Fit the Class-T fuse and the MRBF. Reconnect. Pair the Ionic app and record voltage ___ V, state of charge ___ %, temperature ___ C (into checks, CK02/CK03 as they apply).

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Backbone weekend, 5 of 5: start, charge, voltage drop, run it
note: Start it. Charging voltage at the battery at 2,000 rpm: the reading, in V - expect 13.8-14.6; if it does not charge, stop - alternator or excitation (F15 fixes excitation at E39). Voltage drop while cranking (assistant on the key): battery + post to starter stud the reading, in V, battery - post to engine block the reading, in V, each under 0.5 V - near 0.5 means a bad crimp. Run it - idle, rev, every factory circuit working exactly as before, on a new backbone. No driving: the interior is out until E35 (D-387).

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Dash node 1: lay it out with the parts in hand and cut the carrier panels
note: Inside a cardboard outline of C1's M-1 spaces place the PMU, the two busbars, blocks A and B, the inline holders, the relay sockets (rx7.py sql 02-PROJECTS/01-electrical "select id from relays where location='Dash node'" - K1 K2 K3 K4 K11 K12 K13), the wake strip, the perfboard (P134) and the wideband gauge. Rules: low and close to the floor; the PMU lever arc clear; 60 mm behind every receptacle; blocks reachable; the always-hot busbar covered; PMU stood off for airflow; no bare aluminium against a live stud. Mock the panels in cardboard IN THE CAR first; then cut, deburr, paint (panel stock P090 from C2).

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Dash node 2: mount everything and label every position
note: PMU on three M6 stand-offs; covered always-hot busbar beside the stud; ground bus beside pin 25; blocks A and B; the sealed inline holders; the relay sockets; the 8-position barrier strip (P068 - full: seven wake inputs + the rail); the perfboard. Receptacle clips (P030) along the panel edge grouped by leg. Node labels from E6 beside every relay socket and fuse position, empty ones included.

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Dash node 3: the wake network and the two sense stages
note: Seven 1N5819 on the strip, band (cathode) toward the common rail (N38); rail to pin 7; 10 kOhm rail to ground bus. The two NPN sense stages (door, A8) on the perfboard with the base-network values A10 writes into the record for D-368's baselines - not the v2 values. The two 100 kOhm bias resistors from pin 15 to pins 35 and 22. Then CK12 on the bench before the node goes in the car.

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Dash node 4: terminate the 39-way PMU connector
note: Cavity order from rx7.py sql 02-PROJECTS/01-electrical "select * from pins"; mark cavity 1 with the paint pen first. Strip, crimp the SICMA terminal (2.8 mm large for the heavy pins, 1.5 mm for the rest - per pins), tug, insert until it clicks, tug again; 18 in of wire on every pin; label each wire before cutting the next. Secondary lock on; pull every wire - none may move; latch the lever once fully to prove the arc is clear. It is terminated once and never reopened.

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Dash node 5: every node conductor, every receptacle
note: Run every row of rx7.py sql 02-PROJECTS/01-electrical "select * from node_conductors" - including the ones since v2: N73 road-speed supply, N74 the CAN2 120 Ohm terminator AT THE NODE (D-346), N75 F22 to DP-DCU 1 (D-355), N76-N78, N79 F13, N80-N83 the post links, N84 mirror heat from DP-DCU-B 9 to L4-P 4 (D-369), N85/N86 the release branch and select lines (D-370). O15 now feeds L3-P 2 only (D-369). Every splice a sealed crimp butt splice. Land every leg wire on its receptacle pin per cavities; sealing plug in every PLUG cavity; wedgelocks. Dust caps: the branch-end receptacles get theirs at E20-E23. DP-ICU-A/B are 150 mm tails into the ICU's DT13s (D-270); DP-DCU and DP-DCU-B are tails to the centre stack ending in DT06 plugs, dust-capped (P140, D-362) until the DCU plugs in at E26 (D-374).

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Dash node 6: continuity, isolation, relays, fuses, photos
note: Continuity: each of the 39 cavities reaches every receptacle cavity, relay terminal or strip position the tables say, and nothing else (meter on beeper; touch three places it must NOT reach). Isolation: nothing plugged in, every adjacent pair of power cavities and each power cavity to the ground bus reads open (> 1 MOhm) - any reading is a stray strand. Fit relays K1 K2 K11 K12 K13 (P003) and the fuses per rx7.py sql 02-PROJECTS/01-electrical "select id,rating,block,state from fuses"; empty positions stay empty and labelled (K3/K4 are the luxury package's, LP51). Every node wire labelled at both ends; photograph the finished panels from every angle.

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Dash node 7: the sleeping-current acceptance test (D-280)
note: Node built, PMU asleep, meter in series in the main feed: the reading, in mA. Target 30 mA or less, accept 50 mA or less. Above that, pull wake-strip branches one at a time to find it. Do not close the dash on a failing number - it cannot be re-taken without undoing the install.

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Leg L3 dash: cut, pin, terminate, test
note: For every leg the same loop: lay the route full-scale from the routes table (G13 derives the lengths from C1's M-2); cut every wire in the leg's cavity rows to length + a 150 mm service loop, both ends labelled at once, CAPPED wires exactly like LIVE; crimp the socket contact (leg side = 06-...S housing), cavity order, click, tug; wedgelock; sealing plugs in PLUG cavities; device ends per the device-end rule (rules) using devices; grounds to their star; continuity end to end and the ladder check (switch through every position, ohms at the leg-side cavity vs ladders, within 2 %); tug every crimp; bundle every 150 mm, do NOT final-wrap. L3 specifics: the wiper stalk WASH contact carries both the 1.8 kOhm + diode leg and the plain wire to L3-S2 9; horn 8.2k and both wink NO resistors join onto L3-S1 11; each wink common to dash ground, its NC pole to its own L3-S1 wire; the hazard switch gets its 47k baseline (D-368). Branch ends: L3-CMF, L3-MOD, L3-RDR, dust-capped. L3-S2 3-6 and L3-S3 5-8 run on to DP-DCU-B at the centre stack (D-362).

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Leg L2 front: cut, pin, terminate, test
note: Same loop as E20. Pop-up run feeds land per C1's M-3 ohm check (V-081) - DO NOT pin L2-P before that reading. The 47 kOhm baselines in the back of the L2-S plug to a ground ring on the front star: cavities 1 and 2 (A4/A5) and 3 (A3, D-368). Wiper park terminal L gets the 12k; LB capped. Horns get a ground ring under a mounting bolt. Branch end L2-OAT at the nose, dust-capped. (There is no L2-NZL - D-329.)

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Leg L4 rear + the sill node: cut, pin, terminate, test
note: Same loop as E20. The fuel pump's return is its own 12 AWG to the rear stud, never shared. Sill node: D1/D2 receptacles pinned on the node side, door plugs filled with sealing plugs (RESERVED); ground stud; K5-K8 sockets empty (wired per D-363 - 85 and 87a to ground, 30 to the motor legs, 87 from F8/F9); F8/F9/F14 holders fitted empty (D-283). Door jamb switches: 33k (driver) and 8.2k (passenger) join L4-S 2 at the sill, and the 47k baseline to sill ground there (D-368). L4-M 3/4 run to the hatch and fuel-door solenoids (ring or spade to +; prove each solenoid's ground to the body with the meter) - switched later through K3/K4 (D-370). Branch end L4-RDR, dust-capped. Nothing runs through the door boots.

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Leg L1 engine: cut, pin, terminate, test
note: Same loop as E20. Tach: the shielded cable (P074), drain to the dash node's ground bus at that end only, cut and insulated at the coil end. K9 on the inner fender in its weatherproof socket; its 10 AWG contact wires from F17 to the starter S terminal. Alternator plug: BW to L1-S1 2, WB to L1-S2 8. The ignition suppression condenser P135 on the coil branch at the coil bracket (D-281). L1-S1 9/10 are sealing plugs - the CAN2 terminator is at the dash node now (D-318, D-346). The LS reserves are pinned at the post, not run (D-271).

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Install 1: mount the node, first power-up through 5 A, laptop connected
note: Mount the dash node; prove the lever and every receptacle can be reached. 2 AWG feed to the busbar lug, ground bus to the dash star, NO leg plugged in. First power-up through a 5 A inline bridged across the Class-T block's terminals, so a short melts a 5 A fuse, not 2 AWG. Fit DP-DIAG, laptop over CAN1. Power up with EVERY output disabled: no smoke, module visible. Then swap the 5 A for the Class-T fuse. The laptop is Camden's Windows laptop, kept only to run ECUMaster's PMU client (D-376).

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Install 2: enter the PMU configuration, outputs still disabled
note: The configuration IS the record now (the v2 PMU-CONFIG-SHEET is archived): names and channels from pins, decode tables from inputs + ladders, expressions from logic, the retry classes from rules retry-class (MOTOR_BUS conditional, D-357), wake from rules, CAN from the CAN rows. Save as RevA-01. No limits yet.

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Install 3: plug in L3, the ICU and the DCU; read every input into its window
note: L3 plugged in; the ICU on its two DT13 tails, display on its ribbon; the DCU in its enclosure behind the centre stack on DP-DCU and DP-DCU-B with the panel on its ribbon (D-374) - its luxury loads are not there yet, so its outputs drive capped lines. Every output still disabled: key OFF/ACC/RUN/START, light switch, dimmer, pass, turn, hazard, wiper positions, wash, brake, horn, both winks, doors - write the reading into each decode window, then enter the tables. Every state must land in its window; anything between windows is a wiring fault to fix now. The windows are entered the way inputs.decode says for each input (rules ladder-decode, D-408): A4 and A5 upward, A15 and A16 on conductance - read A15 and A16 at OFF first, to fit k2. Then enter the enable-at limits from pins (enable_a). Still nothing enabled.

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Install 4: L2, L4 + sill and L1 into the car, loads still on the factory harness
note: Route, P-clip, grommet and connect L2, L4 + sill and L1 at both ends with their loads still on the factory harness. Fit F17 and wire K9. The car does not start from E26 until E28 finishes (D-414); it is not driven until E35 (D-387).

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Install 5: migrate every circuit in one stretch, in the migration table's order
note: One stretch, straight after E27, in the migration table's order - it is the test order (D-414): rx7.py sql 02-PROJECTS/01-electrical "select seq,id,circuit,ch from migration order by seq" (MG01 interior lamp first ... MG23 start last). Each circuit is proven alone before the next moves, so a fault shows on the circuit that caused it. The loop for every row: (1) unplug the load at its factory connector, label the factory end MIGRATED + date, tape it back; (2) connect it to the new harness; (3) enable that one output at its enable-at value; (4) operate it and read the live current in the client - that is the real measurement; (5) voltage at the device under load within 0.5 V of the busbar (return side within 0.3 V); (6) record it. On the first one (interior lamp) also set the limit to 2 A and short the output on purpose to watch the soft fuse trip and retry. Set every lamp channel's inrush window before enabling it. MG22 (the meters cutover) waits for F3 (display proven on the bench) and E2 (read the odometer first). The car does not start until MG23 (start) has moved; it is not driven until E35 (D-387).

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Install 6: full function check and save the revision
note: Every migration row done: every circuit in one pass - key out, ACC, RUN, engine running. Wipers LOW/HIGH/INT, park from both speeds, wash only while held; PARK/HEAD/dimmer/pass, pop-ups on HEAD, each wink alone with the key out; crank in P and N only; flasher rate, hazard override, the interior fade. Prove the limp-home procedure once (CK11, recovery RC01-RC08 as corrected by D-367). Save the configuration as a new revision.

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Factory harness out
note: Every migration row done, every factory end labelled MIGRATED, and E29's full function check passed. With the interior still out (D-387, D-411), pull the factory harness out INTACT. Do not cut it. It goes with the factory fuse box, relays and control unit, and the factory cluster leaves with it (D-268). Box it and keep it until after shakedown: it is the fallback if something fails there. There is no week of driving on the disconnected old harness: the car is not driven until the interior is back (E35).

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Shakedown 1: cold, night, wet, long - with logging
note: Cold start on a cold morning with logging on; watch the battery heater in the app and the voltage through crank. Night drive: park, head, high, pass, pop-ups, winks, every lamp, the display's dimming and tell-tales. Wet drive: wipers in every mode, park, wash. A long drive with logging; review every channel's peak current against its limit.

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Shakedown 2: tighten the limits to measured class values
note: Every limit still at its channel cap goes to its measured class value (motors stall x 1.1, lamps x 1.35, resistive cold x 1.2, electronics x 1.5). Record the measured currents in loads.measured_a. Save as a new revision.

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Shakedown 3: re-torque, re-check, final-wrap, seal
note: After the first heat cycles re-torque every lug and stud; re-check the voltage drop on the main feed and ground (E12's numbers). Now final-wrap the engine-bay looms, tie down, seal every grommet - the cabin looms were final-wrapped at E35, before the dash went back (D-387).

stage_title: Then the install plan, in its own order
item: Shakedown 4: the kit that lives in the car
note: Back up the final configuration. In the car: the limp-home kit (recovery RC rows, D-344), a printout of the pins and cavities tables, spare Deutsch contacts, the removal tools and five blade fuses of each value. The electrical project is then ready for CLAUDE.md §6.6 (as-built into 00-CAR, process to the archive).
